To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the optimal shoulder orientation for a dual-arm system is a function of the desired workspace and redundancy of the system, and 2) the optimal shoulder configuration is a function of both workspace and redundancy of each arm.

the upward and forward tilt angle of the shoulders base frame can significantly influence the manipulation performance indices, and the optimal tilt angle for the dual-arm torso is 30° for the upward tilt angle and 0° for the forward tilt angle.

the upward and/or forward orientation of the shoulders base frame in a dual-arm torso structure can be used to enhance the performance of the system in terms of workspace volume, redundancy, global and dual-arm manipulabilities, and inertia ellipsoids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the kinematic analysis of dual-arm systems with different base frames arrangement.
the kinematic analysis of dual-arm systems, and in particular with the design and optimization of the base frame arrangement of the shoulders with respect to the overall torso structure.

the development of a methodology for the kinematic design of the shoulder frame arrangement in a dual-arm torso structure, and to provide a set of guidelines for the design of dual-arm torso structure to achieve optimal kinematic performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a dual-arm humanoid system with upward and forward tilted shoulder frames is not necessarily the best choice for bimanual manipulation, and a dual-arm humanoid with a horizontal shoulder frame orientation may be a better choice.
a shoulder frame orientation of 45 degrees in both directions (upward and forward) would provide the most desired kinematic performance for a humanoid dual-arm system.
a shoulder frame orientation of 30 degrees for upward tilt and 20 degrees for forward tilt would provide the optimal performance for dual-arm manipulation tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a forward tilt angle of the shoulder frames of a dual-arm system can significantly increase the overall and common workspaces, while a larger upward tilt angle would increase the redundancy and global isotropy of the system.
the kinematic performance of the dual-arm system can be significantly improved by the proper design of the torso structure.

a dual-arm humanoid torso should have the shoulders placed at an angle of approximately 30° upward and forward tilt from the vertical torso plane to achieve the best performance in terms of workspace and isotropy, and to have the least redundant degree of freedom.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal configuration of the base frame of the shoulder joints is not necessarily the upward and forward tilt configuration, which is the most common configuration used in dual-arm systems.
, in general, a dual-arm system should be designed such that the shoulders' frames are placed in an orientation that is close to a horizontal plane.
the shoulder frame orientation has a significant effect on the performance indices of the dual-arm torso system and, thus, should not be ignored during the system design process.
